output.revised_prompt:
Edit Image 1 (the first supplied image) into a complete commercial-grade CHAMPAGNE CLASSIC mechanical slot cabinet, using Image 2 only as a reference for functional completeness, finish quality, manufactured thickness, and integrated hardware. Do not copy Image 2's ornate black/gold ornament system, columns, vault motif, gems, or overall silhouette.

Preserve from Image 1: its unique unmistakably wide, low Hollywood-retro silhouette; scalloped champagne-bulb marquee surround; warm coral-red stitched leather; champagne brass/copper trim; tiny jade accents; front-facing casino-floor camera; and upholstered lower cabinet body. Keep the entire cabinet fully visible, uncropped, in a true straight-on front elevation. The cabinet must be noticeably wider and lower than conventional slot machines.

Build a complete physical mechanical slot layout from top to bottom:
1) A broad blank coral leather-and-champagne-brass title marquee integrated beneath the scalloped bulb crown. It must remain totally blank.
2) A separate narrow dark inset counter socket directly below it, framed in cast champagne brass, blank with no digits or text.
3) An extra-large, highly readable warm-ivory 3-by-3 mechanical reel glass: three physical vertical drums/reels and three visible rows, nine clean blank cells total. Add pronounced champagne-brass vertical drum separators, subtle horizontal registration lines, convex glass, substantial cast bezel, screws and believable depth. Absolutely no reel symbols, icons, letters, or numbers.
4) A dedicated narrow dark win/result display below the reels, built into its own brass bezel, entirely blank.
5) A deep sloped coral leather control console with visible polished metal edge rails and real manufactured thickness. Controls must be physical and seated in dedicated built-in sockets, never floating UI: left Turbo key socket; dominant central illuminated Spin dome in warm ivory glass with ruby-red center/accent; right Auto key/lever socket; paired small Bet minus/plus button well; and two long low horizontal brass key sockets for Paytable and Rules. Keep every face completely blank for later code labels—no plus/minus glyphs, words, letters, numbers, icons, logos, or symbols. Differentiate the paired Bet controls only through shape/position or tiny jade/ruby color accents, not markings.
6) Preserve and finish the lower upholstered coral cabinet body, with stitched vertical padding, brass base rails, seams, screws, beveled trim, and stable floor contact. Do not add a vault door or unrelated ornament.

Design language: cheerful glamorous 1930s–1950s Hollywood-retro casino cabinet, warm and inviting rather than dark or formal. Materials should read as production-grade brushed and polished champagne brass, warm copper, coral leather, cream ivory enamel/glass, cast bezels, convex glass, bulb housings, screws, seams, beveled metal edges, and authentic mechanical assembly thickness. Soft glamorous champagne reflections and warm marquee glow. Background may remain a softly blurred warm casino floor, with no people.

Strict text rule: no baked-in words, letters, numbers, glyphs, labels, logos, watermarks, or readable signage anywhere in the image. All marquee, display, reel, and control faces are blank.

Avoid: floating UI, tablet or modern touchscreen appearance, black nightclub styling, dark formal mood, people, hands, banknotes, coins, alcohol, logos, symbols inside reel cells, copied ornamentation from Image 2, cropped cabinet, perspective angle, incomplete controls, or controls floating inside the reel screen. Produce a polished photorealistic production portrait slot-cabinet master background.
